tasks.short: Examine records to locate links in chains of evidence or information.

steps.what: Examine the case records for this evidence chain
Read each source record that holds a coded identifier
Locate repeated links across the detective case records
Decide which links belong in the evidence chain
Write the accepted evidence chain into the case record

tasks.design: She still reads the source records and still decides which link belongs in the evidence chain. A configured query on {OTHER} lists candidate links where the same stored phone or account identifier appears in more than one record. She then writes that accepted evidence chain into the case record herself. The query does not summarise the records and does not predict an offence.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same phone or account number sat in separate records, and she compared them by eye because no field was marked as the match key.
tasks.enabler_now: The records officer already stores those identifiers as fields on the case record, so a query can list the repeats.
tasks.still_hard: Prose with no coded identifier still has nothing to match, and a repeated number can be a switchboard. She still reads the source.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a shared front-desk number from a number that actually ties two records in this case.
tasks.altitude: She still decides which link is real. She spends less time hunting the same coded identifier by hand. Reading the source and writing the chain stay hers.

reach.task: List candidate links where the same stored identifier appears in more than one record.
reach.learn: Which repeated number is only a shared switchboard.

evidence.claim: Matching one stored identifier across records is a query. It does not need a model when the identifier is already a field.
BEAR tags sentences by topic and orders documents. Summarising was rejected because details matter, so the detective still reads the source records.
A solely automated decision with an adverse effect needs prior human intervention. She decides which link stands before it is written into the case record.
Offence prediction solely from profiling is banned. The candidate list is a repeat of stored identifiers, not a prediction of an offence.
A crime-forecast tool was phased out on 1 December 2025 after an evaluation. This design does not forecast offences.
Works-council consent is required for staff monitoring. The match log is not used to score the detective.

assumptions: The focal role is the detective. The records officer and the intelligence analyst are other roles and are not in her shares.

Phone numbers and account identifiers used by the query are already fields on the case record in {OTHER}. The records officer entered them when the record was filed. That entry is not part of this task.
If the identifier is only in prose, the query leaves it off the candidate list and she still finds it while reading the source in s2.
An intelligence analyst keeps the list of fields the query may match. She does not. That upkeep is other-role time and is not deducted from her net.
The model-needed prior overstates this step. A query does not need a model. Unguided prose stays in her reading.
The match log is not used to score her. Works-council consent is in the build because a monitoring use of the same log would need it.
Writing the accepted chain is her own entry into the case record. It is not a send outside the force, and it is not counted as time saved.
unknowns: Whether this unit's case records already store phone and account identifiers as fields.
What share of the records in a typical file are prose with no coded identifier.
research_questions: On a recent file, how long did she spend comparing coded identifiers by eye, as against reading the source?

already_counted.description: Reading the source records and deciding which links stand stay in s2 and s4.

incremental.description: An intelligence analyst keeps the list of identifier fields the query may match. The detective does not keep that list.
No match-field upkeep falls back to her. Prose with no coded identifier stays in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the hunt for a coded identifier that is already a field is removed. Low 6: a thin file where most records are untagged prose, so she still reads almost everything in s2. High 16: phones and account numbers are usually stored, while she still reads the source and still decides which link stands. High stays under the 22 point net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and serve search and arrest warrants.

steps.what: Read the case facts behind this search warrant
Write the grounds for the search or arrest
Copy stored header fields onto the warrant form
Check the search warrant grounds against the case facts
Magistrate signs the search or arrest warrant
Serve the signed search or arrest warrant

tasks.design: She still writes the grounds for the search or arrest, a magistrate still signs, and she still serves the warrant in person. A configured copy moves party name, address, and offence from fields already on the case record in {OTHER} onto the warrant form in {DOCS}. The copy leaves the grounds blank. It does not decide whether the search is justified.
tasks.previous_blocker: The warrant form mixed party headers with the facts that justify the search, so she retyped the headers with the grounds.
tasks.enabler_now: Party name, address, and offence are already fields on the case record. A form can copy those and leave the grounds blank for her.
tasks.still_hard: The grounds are her judgement. A wrong address is hard to undo. The magistrate still signs, and she still serves the warrant at the door.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which facts are enough for the magistrate and which detail would overstate the case.
tasks.altitude: She still writes the grounds and still serves the warrant. She stops retyping party name, address, and offence that are already on the case record.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
reach.task: Say which warrant facts are headers and which are the grounds.
reach.learn: A copied address is not a reason for the search.

evidence.claim: Copying party name, address, and offence from stored case fields onto a warrant form is a field copy. It does not write the grounds.
A randomised trial found that police reports were not written faster with a drafting aid. The warrant grounds stay the detective's writing.
A solely automated decision with an adverse effect needs prior human intervention. The magistrate signs the warrant before it is served.

assumptions: The focal role is the detective. The magistrate who signs is another role. The forms officer who keeps the header map is another role. Neither is in her net.

Party name, address, and offence used as headers were entered on the case record by the reporting officer when the case was opened. That entry is not part of this task. If a header field is blank, the copy leaves it blank and she fills it while checking s4.
A forms officer keeps which fields are headers and which stay blank for the grounds. She does not keep that map.
Serving the warrant is done in person to a person outside the force. It is bound to the signed warrant and is not shortened.
The grounds are not drafted by a model. The trial that found reports were not written faster is why that writing stays hers.
unknowns: Whether party name, address, and offence are already separate fields on this unit's case record.
How often a header field is blank on the day she prepares the warrant.
research_questions: On the last ten warrants, how long was the header retype as against writing the grounds and serving at the door?

already_counted.description: Writing the grounds, checking them, and serving the warrant stay in s2, s4, and s6.
The magistrate's signature stays in s5 and is not her time.

incremental.description: A forms officer keeps which warrant fields are headers and which stay blank for the grounds. The detective does not keep that map.
No form-map upkeep falls back to her. A blank header is caught in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype of party name, address, and offence is removed, and only when those fields are already stored. Low 3: several headers are blank, so she still types them inside the check. High 8: headers are usually filled, while the grounds, the magistrate's signature, and service at the door stay. High is under the net of about 11 points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Obtain summary of incident from officer in charge at crime scene, taking care to avoid disturbing evidence.

steps.what: Obtain the incident summary from the officer in charge
Walk the crime scene without disturbing evidence
Write the incident summary the officer gave

tasks.design: She still obtains the incident summary from the officer in charge at the scene, and she still walks the crime scene without disturbing evidence. The typed incident summary stays her writing in {DOCS}. Nothing in the visit is handed to a machine.
tasks.previous_blocker: The summary is spoken at the scene, and the care not to disturb evidence is in how she walks. Nothing in that visit is a field a query can fill.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes the scene visit shorter. The note afterwards is still her writing.
tasks.still_hard: She has to hear the officer in charge and see the scene without moving evidence.
tasks.human_edge: She notices what the officer's summary leaves out, and she knows which item must not be touched.
tasks.altitude: The scene visit does not change. She still takes the summary from the officer in charge and still walks the scene herself.

reach.task: Give the incident summary at the scene without moving evidence.
reach.learn: Which part of the summary is what the officer saw, and which part is still unchecked.

evidence.claim: The incident summary is spoken by the officer in charge at the scene. A later typed note does not shorten that visit.
A randomised trial found that police reports were not written faster with a drafting aid. The scene note stays her writing and is not counted as time saved.

assumptions: The officer in charge is a colleague at the scene. The talk is not a send outside the force.
The note in s3 is her own writing of what she heard. It is not a version sent to a court, so it has no separate release gate.
No field list is added. The officer's briefing already happens and is not new work.
The vanish prior is not a reason to shorten the walk. The design does not change the visit.
unknowns: How often the officer in charge is still at the scene when she arrives.
research_questions: What share of this task is the conversation and the walk, as against typing the note later?

already_counted.description: Hearing the officer and walking the scene without disturbing evidence stay in s1 and s2.

incremental.description: No field list is added. The officer in charge already gives the summary, and that briefing is not new work.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The summary is spoken at the scene and the walk is how she avoids disturbing evidence. The design leaves both unchanged, so the saving stays at zero on a short scene and on a long one.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Testify before grand juries concerning criminal activity investigations.

steps.what: Read the investigations file before grand-jury testimony
Copy stored exhibit dates into a prep list
Check those dates against the investigation file
Meet the prosecutor about the testimony scope
Testify before the grand jury on the activity

tasks.design: She still reads the investigations file, still meets the prosecutor, and still testifies before the grand jury. A configured copy lists exhibit dates and exhibit ids already stored on the case record in {OTHER} into a prep list in {DOCS}. She checks those dates against the file. The list does not suggest what she should say, and she does not send it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exhibit dates were copied by hand into a prep list because they lived on the exhibit record, not in one list for the hearing.
tasks.enabler_now: The evidence clerk already stores exhibit dates and exhibit ids on the case record. A query can list them. It cannot say what she should tell the jury.
tasks.still_hard: She still answers questions in the room. A date on a list is not the testimony.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which date the prosecutor will be asked about, and when to stop.
tasks.altitude: She still testifies herself. She spends less time copying exhibit dates that are already on the case record. What she says stays her decision.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
reach.task: Agree which part of the file she will speak to, before the hearing.
reach.learn: A list of exhibit dates is not a script for the jury.

evidence.claim: Copying stored exhibit dates and exhibit ids into a list is a field copy. It does not draft what she should say.
A randomised trial found that police reports were not written faster with a drafting aid. Spoken testimony is not treated as a drafted report, and no drafting time is counted as saved.
A tool that scores the reliability of evidence is high-risk. The prep list is dates and exhibit ids, not a score.

assumptions: The focal role is the detective. The evidence clerk who entered the exhibit dates, and who keeps the field list, is another role. That entry is not part of this task.
If an exhibit has no stored date, the copy leaves it off the list and she still sees it while reading the file in s1.
The prosecutor meeting is a talk with a colleague about scope. It is not a document sent outside the force.
Testimony is spoken in the room. It is not a versioned document, so it has no release gate. She does not file or send the prep list.
The list is not used to score her, and it does not score the evidence.
unknowns: Whether exhibit dates and exhibit ids are already fields on this unit's case record.
How many exhibits a typical hearing covers.
research_questions: On the last hearings, how long was the copy of exhibit dates as against reading the file and time in the room?

already_counted.description: Reading the file, checking dates, meeting the prosecutor, and testifying stay in s1, s3, s4, and s5.

incremental.description: An evidence clerk keeps which exhibit fields the prep list may copy. The detective does not keep that list.
No exhibit-field upkeep falls back to her. A missing date stays in her reading of the file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the copy of exhibit dates that are already stored is removed. Low 2: a short hearing with few stored dates, so almost all the day is reading, the prosecutor, and testimony. High 5: many exhibits already have dates, while she still checks them and still testifies. High stays under the 6 point net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still decides which link is real, still serves the warrant, and still gives the evidence in person. Less time is spent hunting the same identifier by hand or retyping warrant headers.
reach: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
skills_to_grow: Tell a repeated phone number from a real link in the evidence chain.
Write warrant grounds the magistrate can sign.
Testify from the file rather than from a prep list.
role.ambitious_version: On a case with coded phones and account numbers, the candidate links and the warrant headers are waiting. She still reads the records, still writes the grounds, still walks the scene, and still testifies herself.
